title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens §43, a digression on (nonabelian) 1-cocycles of cyclic groups. The crossed-out first title was 'Retour sur les rotations', and the page number 350 is added in the margin.

Setup: let π be a group and ρ an automorphism with ρ^n = id. Then Z/nZ acts on π, giving the semidirect product π~ = π ⋊ Z/nZ and an extension 1 → π → π~ → Z/nZ → 1. This extension has a canonical splitting sending 1 mod n to ρ. Inside π~, ρ acts by inner conjugation: ρ(g) = ρ g ρ^{-1}.

Claim: splittings of the extension correspond bijectively to elements ρ' of π~ lying over the generator ρ̇ with ρ'^n = 1. Writing ρ' = ρ'_g = gρ with g ∈ π, one computes
(gρ)^n = g · ρ(g) · ρ²(g) ⋯ ρ^{n-1}(g) · ρ^n.
Since ρ^n = 1 in π~, condition (6) becomes the boxed norm equation
(8) g ρ(g) ρ²(g) ⋯ ρ^{n-1}(g) = 1.
This is the nonabelian 1-cocycle condition for Z/n acting on π: a cocycle is determined by its value g on the generator, subject to the 'norm' being trivial.

The next page continues the standard theory. π-conjugation of splittings corresponds to ρ-twisted conjugation g ↦ α g ρ(α)^{-1}. Conjugacy classes of splittings correspond to H^1(Z/n, π), and the trivial class consists of the coboundaries α ρ(α)^{-1}.

Purpose in context: the preceding pages study elements ξ = λ ρ(λ)^{-1} in π̂_{0,3} (and in SL(2,Ẑ)') satisfying an 'équation en ξ'. Here ρ is the order-3 rotation of the three punctures of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, and n = 3 or 2. The equations of the 'équation des lacets' are of exactly this norm form, e.g. the hexagon-type relation f(x,y)x^m · f(z,x)z^m · f(y,z)y^m = 1. The digression recasts them as the condition that gρ is a torsion element lifting the rotation, i.e. as nonabelian H^1 of a cyclic group. Elements of the form λρ(λ)^{-1} are then exactly the coboundaries. The question on the previous page — whether a solution over λ_0 lifts to one of the form λρ(λ)^{-1} — becomes a question about liftability of cohomology classes and of the trivial class.
errors: No mathematical errors. The computation (gρ)^n = g ρ(g) ⋯ ρ^{n-1}(g) ρ^n = g ρ(g) ⋯ ρ^{n-1}(g) is correct, as is the bijection between splittings and order-dividing-n lifts of the generator.
Minor labelling slip: the semidirect product equation is labelled '(1)' a second time; it should be (2).

ideas.what: Splittings of π ⋊ Z/n ↔ elements g with g ρ(g) ⋯ ρ^{n-1}(g) = 1; conjugacy of splittings ↔ twisted conjugacy g ↦ α g ρ(α)^{-1}; trivial class = coboundaries α ρ(α)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian H^1 of a cyclic group (norm condition for cocycles)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Serre, Cohomologie galoisienne; standard group cohomology)
ideas.where_published: Standard material; Grothendieck uses nonabelian H^1 throughout SGA and Giraud's framework, but this exact cyclic-group digression is not in published texts as far as known

ideas.what: Viewing the rotation-type 'loop equations' (GT-like hexagon/2-cycle relations) as cocycle conditions, i.e. as torsion lifts of the rotation of the three punctures
ideas.modern_name: Interpretation of the GT relations as preservation of torsion elements / conjugacy of finite-order elements (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the Longue Marche manuscripts; not in Esquisse beyond general remarks

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a textbook account of nonabelian 1-cocycles for a cyclic group. Its interest is only contextual: it prepares a cohomological reformulation of the loop equations in π̂_{0,3}. That reformulation is close in spirit to the known torsion-element interpretation of the GT relations.

Line after (3): 'On note ρ̇ le générateur de Z/nZ, et on identifie ρ̇ à son image dans π~, par le scindage canonique (4)'. The stray 'Z' is an aborted start of (4).
Before (8): 'et on trouve donc que pour les g ∈ π l'équation (6) se récrit ainsi'.
